newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila C. Bank says it net dollar seller.
newsitem.headline: Manila C. Bank says it net dollar seller.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank was a net seller of dollars totalling of $137.5 million as of 0915 GMT, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson told reporters on Wednesday.
The monetary authority had been forced to intervene in the market after Thailand said it would allow a managed float of its currency.
As of that time, Singson said volume had reached $1.026 billion, of which $545.3 million were purchases and sales of the Central Bank.
"This is a typical case where intervention is justified now that there is speculative attack arising from what happened in Thailand," Singson said.
"I think this is only an initial reaction from the change in Thailand's exchange rate policy. I am confident things will eventually settle down," he said.
Turnover in the foreign exchange market was close to double the previous record set in May. The government has repeatedly been forced to protect the peso from the impact of the Thai baht's woes.
